turns.prompt_text: how do you cook an eggplant safely
turns.response_html:
To cook eggplant safely, heat it thoroughly to break down solanine, a natural toxin that can cause digestive upset if consumed raw. Follow these essential steps for the best results:

  • Prep: Wash the skin and trim the green cap. While not a safety requirement, "sweating" slices with salt for 20 minutes can draw out bitterness and prevent the flesh from soaking up excessive oil.
  • Cooking: Roast, grill, or sauté until the texture is completely soft and creamy. Undercooked eggplant remains tough, spongy, and difficult to digest.
  • Storage: Keep cooked eggplant in the fridge for up to 5 days or freeze it for longer storage. If the raw flesh has dark brown spots or a slimy texture, discard it to avoid spoilage.
